The five decisions

  1. 01 Can you buy at all? Eligibility
  2. 02 Should you buy? Motive
  3. 03 Which city? City
  4. 04 Which property? Asset

Read left to right. A "no" at any layer ends the purchase — that is the point of doing them in order.

Why this exists

The information is not missing. The order is.

English-language material about Chinese property is abundant and almost entirely unstructured. Every source answers one question; nobody tells you which question comes first, or when to walk away.

01 — Sequence

Order changes the answer

Eligibility, motive, city, asset, closing. Ask them out of order and you will fall in love with an apartment in a city where you cannot legally buy it — the most expensive mistake in this market, and the most common.

02 — Veto

Someone has to say no

Your agent is paid when you buy. Your lawyer is paid either way. Nobody in the chain is paid to tell you to wait, so this site is written to help you conclude "not yet" as quickly as possible.

03 — Verification

Paths, not conclusions

We do not tell you a city is fine. We tell you which counter to stand at, which three questions to ask, and what a written answer looks like — because the rules are applied locally.
